_doc: Conversations (DialogueManager). Option kinds: plain, persuade, intimidate, bribe, empathy, lie, negotiate, refuse. effects: rel, rel_other, fear, flag, money, debt, rep, faction, heat, path, quest, consequence, appearance_char, appearance_player, supplies, ending.

start.text: You're the new one renting Kaspar's storeroom. Hm. You hold the scalpel like a pen. Good. Pens don't shake. ...Mine do, now.
start.speaker: npc

options.text: Who are you?
Your hands. How long have they been like that?
I don't need a lecture. I need customers.

who.text: Ilse Hartmann. I cut people in this district for thirty years. Before that I cut them for a company that paid better and asked worse questions.
who.speaker: npc

options.text: Which company?
Then teach me.

company.text: ...Lyra. Biocomp. Don't make that face; everyone with a medical licence worked for Lyra once. Some of us stopped.
company.speaker: npc

company_no.text: One that doesn't exist for people like us. Next question.
company_no.speaker: npc

hands.text: Since the implant in my ulnar nerve started rejecting. I built half the good ones on the market and I can't afford my own revision. Funny, isn't it.
hands.speaker: npc

hands_cold.text: Long enough. Don't play nurse with me.
hands_cold.speaker: npc

rude.text: Customers come to people who don't kill them. Learn that first and the rest follows.
rude.speaker: npc

teach.text: Here: my old retractor set. It's older than you and steadier than me. One condition. If a patient ever comes in with a lattice under the skull, fine grey threads, fever that comes and goes like static, you call me. Before anyone else. Promise me.
teach.speaker: npc

options.text: I promise.
What is a 'lattice'?
Depends what it's worth to you.

lattice.text: A mistake I made a long time ago. Promise first. Questions later.
lattice.speaker: npc

options.text: Alright. I promise.

lattice_no.text: Something you'll recognise if you ever see it. Promise.
lattice_no.speaker: npc

options.text: I promise.

paid.text: Mercenary. Good, actually. Mercenaries keep their contracts. Take the money and the tools.
paid.speaker: npc

promise.text: Do three clean jobs and come find me in the Old Caldera. I'll show you how to close a wound so it stays closed.
promise.speaker: npc

start.text: Lovely little room. Lovely little operation. Lovely little problem: the building's worth more since you moved your blood in. Rent goes up. Two hundred, today, for the privilege.
start.speaker: npc

options.text: Fine. Two hundred.
You can wait till the end of the week.
Touch my door again and you'll need a ripper yourself.
I'll patch up your collectors for free instead.

paid.text: See? We're friends now. Friends pay on time.
paid.speaker: npc

waits.text: A week. Not a day more. I'm a patient man; my interest isn't.
waits.speaker: npc

nowait.text: End of the week is when I sell your lease to a noodle franchise. Two hundred goes on your tab.
nowait.speaker: npc

scared.text: ...Charming. We'll talk again. When you've cooled down.
scared.speaker: npc

laughs.text: Ha. Two hundred plus a nuisance fee. It's on your tab, butcher.
laughs.speaker: npc

service.text: Free? Nothing's free. But my lads do get cut a lot... Fine. Rent stays where it is, and you never ask what they were doing when they got hurt.
service.speaker: npc

start.text: A week, I said. You're breathing, the room's breathing. Pay me what's owed.
start.speaker: npc

options.text: Here. Two hundred and fifty, for your patience.
I can't. Put it on the tab.
Lie: Lyra's paying me next week. Big contract.

variants.text: A week, I said. And I hear you charge the desperate double. Lovely. Then you can certainly pay me what's owed.
A week, I said. I hear you treat people for free. Charming. I don't. Pay me what's owed.

ok.text: A pleasure doing business with someone sensible.
ok.speaker: npc

tab.text: Three hundred on the tab. Eight percent a day. I do love arithmetic.
tab.speaker: npc

lie_ok.text: Lyra. Well. Then I can wait for a corporate cheque.
lie_ok.speaker: npc

lie_bad.text: Lyra doesn't sign contracts with people who rent storerooms. Three-fifty on the tab, liar.
lie_bad.speaker: npc

start.text: My associates broke a few things on the way in. Clumsy lads. They'll be less clumsy if we're friends again.
start.speaker: npc

options.text: How much to make them careful?
Get out. Next time I see them, they're on my table, not standing.

out.text: ...We'll see who's standing. Not today, though.
out.speaker: npc

wreck.text: Pity about your lamp. And your till.
wreck.speaker: npc

d_teo_ask.title: The Kid With The Soldering Iron

start.text: Hi. Sorry. Hi. I'm Teo. I fix people's implants on my floor with a soldering iron and I'm going to kill someone if I keep doing it alone. Do you... need hands?
start.speaker: npc

options.text: Show me your hands.
Why should I trust a dropout?
I can't pay you.

hands.text: They're steady. Mostly. I did forty eye-port cleanings last winter. Nobody went blind. One person went... a bit blurry.
hands.speaker: npc

why.text: Because I'd rather be supervised than be the guy kids go to because he's cheap. I've got one rule: I won't put chrome into kids. Ever.
why.speaker: npc

why_bad.text: ...You shouldn't, probably. But I'm here and nobody else is.
why_bad.speaker: npc

nopay.text: Thirty-five a day. I'll eat noodles. I've eaten worse.
nopay.speaker: npc

terms.text: So? Do I get a coat?
terms.speaker: npc

options.text: Welcome aboard. Hiring board's yours, Teo.
No kids. Agreed. That's my rule too.
Not now. Maybe when I can pay.

yes.text: Okay. Okay! I'll be on your hiring board tomorrow; the paperwork's in my head. Thank you.
yes.speaker: npc

later.text: Sure. I'll keep my name on the board. In case.
later.speaker: npc

start.text: Rook says you're good with a blade. That's nice. My crews bleed on this street every night, and every night someone's got to choose: help Mother, or be a problem for Mother. Which are you?
start.speaker: npc

options.text: What does helping look like?
I don't pick sides. I pick up scalpels.
Get out of my clinic.

variants.text: The crews already call you their doc. Rook says you're good with a blade, and my boys come back stitched straight. So let's make it official: help Mother, or be a problem for Mother.
The Sump says you treat anyone for nothing. Sweet. My crews are anyone too. Help Mother, or be a problem for Mother. Which are you?
Rook says you patch corporate suits down here. Brave. On this street, every night, someone's got to choose: help Mother, or be a problem for Mother.

terms.text: Fifty a day, paid to Rook. Or: my wounded come in through the back, you patch them, no names, no Aegis. Your choice which coin.
terms.speaker: npc

options.text: Fifty a day. I'll pay.
I'll be the crews' medic. No money changes hands.
Half my bench already wears your colours. We're square.
How about twenty-five?
I'll take my chances with Aegis.

neutral_line.text: Everyone picks a side, Doctor. Some just pick late.
neutral_line.speaker: npc

pay.text: Simple. Rook will come by. Smile at him; he's sensitive.
pay.speaker: npc

medic.text: Better. Money can be stolen. Debts of blood can't. You'll see my people tonight.
medic.speaker: npc

haggle.text: Twenty-five. You've got nerve. I like nerve, in small doses.
haggle.speaker: npc

nohaggle.text: Fifty. That was me being generous.
nohaggle.speaker: npc

aegis.text: Aegis. Then Aegis can sit in your waiting room when we come.
aegis.speaker: npc

bold.text: Hm. Brave, or stupid. We'll find out together.
bold.speaker: npc

laugh.text: Out of your clinic? Sweetheart, this whole street is mine. Enjoy the next few nights.
laugh.speaker: npc

square.text: ...Square. You've earned that word. Don't wear it out.
square.speaker: npc

start.text: Mother sends regards. And a lesson. Lights off, everyone on the floor.
start.speaker: npc

options.text: Take what you want. Nobody gets hurt.
Fight back.
Tell Mother I'll treat her crews. For free.

fight.text: ...Alright. Alright! We're going. You're crazy, you know that?
fight.speaker: npc

hurt.text: Brave. Stupid. Don't bleed on your own floor, Doctor.
hurt.speaker: npc

deal.text: Free. Huh. I'll tell her. She might even like you.
deal.speaker: npc

start.text: Darling. You're getting a name, which is bad for a person in your line, and good for me. I have a courier who needs an optic nobody can trace. Interested?
start.speaker: npc

options.text: I'm already the fence on this street. Fifty-fifty or I go direct.
What's the cut?
Untraceable means stolen.
I don't do black chrome.

variants.text: Darling. You already move more unregistered chrome than half my contacts, which is bad for a person in your line and good for me. Let's make it official.

cut_good.text: Sixty-forty, your way, because I like your face. Install anything off my shelf and I'll send the courier's fee. Clean, quiet, done.
cut_good.speaker: npc

cut_bad.text: Seventy-thirty, mine, because I can. Still interested?
cut_bad.speaker: npc

options.text: Fine.
No.

stolen.text: Liberated. From a Lyra freight lift. Nobody died. Well. Nobody who mattered to Lyra.
stolen.speaker: npc

options.text: Then I'm in.
I'll pass.

stolen_no.text: Darling, everything in this city is stolen. Including the city.
stolen_no.speaker: npc

options.text: Then I'm in.
I'll pass.

no.text: Principles. Adorable. They're expensive; call me when you can't afford them.
no.speaker: npc

start.text: Inspector Moor, Civic Medical Board. You're unlicensed, unregistered, and two of your patients are in my files with 'seizure, unknown cause'. You can explain, or I can write.
start.speaker: npc

options.text: Bribe: three hundred and you never came.
I keep my patients alive. That's more than your board does.
Here: my patient records. Take what you need.
Seizures... with fever that comes and goes? I've seen that too.
Look at my waiting room. Shut me down and they go to nobody.

variants.text: Inspector Moor, Civic Medical Board. Half the Sump swears you're a saint. Saints still need licences. You're unlicensed, unregistered, and two of your patients turned up at Mercy General seizing.
Inspector Moor, Civic Medical Board. I've been counting your dead, Doctor. Unlicensed, unregistered, and two more of your patients turned up at Mercy General seizing.
Inspector Moor, Civic Medical Board. Your waiting room is a crew clubhouse with gauze. You're unlicensed, unregistered, and two of your patients turned up at Mercy General seizing.

bribed.text: ...I'll file this as a wasted afternoon.
bribed.speaker: npc

bribe_fail.text: Attempting to bribe a Board inspector. Thank you; that's the easiest report I'll write all month.
bribe_fail.speaker: npc

convinced.text: Alive. Hm. Keep them alive and keep them out of my files.
convinced.speaker: npc

variants.text: ...I've seen your bench. Fine. Keep them alive and keep them out of my files. I never saw your back door.

fine.text: Two hundred, unlicensed practice, payable now. Next time it's closure.
fine.speaker: npc

records.text: Cooperation. Rare down here. I'll remember this. So will your patients, if anyone else finds out.
records.speaker: npc

fever.text: ...Twelve cases this month. All Sump. All with neural chrome nobody admits selling. The Board says 'drug interaction'. I don't believe the Board.
fever.speaker: npc

start.text: I took your money. My daughter's tuition chip took it next. And now someone at the Board is asking why I keep losing your file.
start.speaker: npc

options.text: Then lose it one more time. Here's five hundred.
Let's stop pretending. What do you actually need?
You took a bribe. Report me and you go down too.

owned.text: ...Bought and paid for. Don't make me regret it more than I already do.
owned.speaker: npc

truth.text: I need someone in the Sump who'll tell me when the fever cases come in. Not to arrest. To count.
truth.speaker: npc

burned.text: Go ahead. I'll confess; you'll close. Let's see who sleeps better.
burned.speaker: npc

start.text: So you're the backroom saint. Your prices are killing my margins. Here's a gift: join me. My name on the door, your hands on the table, sixty percent of nothing is better than a hundred percent of a closed clinic.
start.speaker: npc

options.text: Partners, then. Equal names.
Lie: Lyra already offered me more.
Get out of my clinic, Silas.

partner.text: Equal. Fine. Equal is still better than drowning. My clinic sends you its overflow; you send me your hard cases. We both get rich slowly.
partner.speaker: npc

sub.text: Equal? You have one table. I have nine. Sixty-forty or nothing.
sub.speaker: npc

options.text: Then nothing.
...Sixty-forty.

rattled.text: ...Lyra. Huh. Then I'll be watching who walks through your door.
rattled.speaker: npc

called.text: Lyra doesn't even know your name. But now I know you lie. Interesting.
called.speaker: npc

war.text: Have it your way. Supplies get expensive in a war.
war.speaker: npc

start.text: Heard your supply drop went into the canal. Tragic. My offer still stands, at worse terms.
start.speaker: npc

options.text: Ruin him: tell Mother he's been selling her crews' chrome to Aegis.
Fine. Your terms.
Walk away.

ruined.text: ...What did you do? Mother's people are at my doors. You absolute— this isn't over.
ruined.speaker: npc

nope.text: Mother laughed you out of the room, I hear. Shame.
nope.speaker: npc

leave.text: Then lose more supplies. I can do this all year.
leave.speaker: npc

start.text: Aegis caught three of mine in the Belt. They're bleeding out in your doorway. I'm not asking.
start.speaker: npc

options.text: Bring them in. All three. No charge.
I'll take them. Triple rate.
I'm not dying for your war. Take them somewhere else.
Call Aegis. They pay bounties.

saved.text: ...All three breathing. I don't forget, Doctor. Not the good things either.
saved.speaker: npc

paid.text: Triple. You're a businesswoman. Fine. They live; you eat.
paid.speaker: npc

refused.text: Two of them died on the stairs. I'll remember which stairs.
refused.speaker: npc

sold.text: You... You called them. Run, Doctor. Run fast.
sold.speaker: npc

start.text: Doctor. Cassian Voss, Lyra Biocomp, clinical outreach. I'll be brief because your time is valuable and mine is billed. We have a lattice stabiliser - neural, gentle, wonderful for tremor and grief. We'd like it in the Sump. Your hands, our product, two thousand on signing.
start.speaker: npc

options.text: Two thousand. Done.
Make it four.
Your people already trust my table. That's worth four.
A stabiliser for grief? What's it really for?
No. I don't test products on my patients.

variants.text: Doctor. Cassian Voss, Lyra Biocomp, clinical outreach. Several of our people speak well of your discretion, so I'll be brief.

signed.text: Wonderful. Kits arrive tomorrow. Do report anything... unusual. Fevers, for example. We care very much about fevers.
signed.speaker: npc

signed_more.text: You negotiate like someone who's been poor. Four. Report anything unusual.
signed_more.speaker: npc

firm.text: Two, Doctor. I'm generous, not stupid.
firm.speaker: npc

options.text: Two, then.
No deal.

slip.text: Grief... is a signal problem. THREAD - ah, the stabiliser - re-routes it. It's a trial, technically. Every miracle is, technically.
slip.speaker: npc

options.text: A trial on people who can't sue. Get out.
Then pay me like a trial site. Four thousand.

smooth.text: For exactly what the leaflet says, Doctor. Would you like a leaflet?
smooth.speaker: npc

options.text: Sign me up.
No.

refused.text: Pity. The Sump will get its stabilisers either way. Only the hands change.
refused.speaker: npc

start.text: ...Doctor? The patients from the Lyra kits. Four of them. Fever, then the static - like a radio between stations, in their heads. One of them stopped talking. I've had it for two years. I know what it sounds like.
start.speaker: npc

options.text: Who are you?
Can it be removed?

variants.text: ...Doctor? You're the one who cut Bed 14 loose. She told us. The patients from the Lyra kits: four of them. Fever, then the static, like a radio between stations. One stopped talking. I've had it for two years. I know what it sounds like.

noor.text: Noor Sayeh. Lyra called me 'Patient Zero' when they thought I couldn't hear. I can hear everything. That's the problem.
noor.speaker: npc

remove.text: Maybe. By someone who knows what it is. There's an old surgeon in the Caldera who used to wake up screaming the word THREAD.
remove.speaker: npc

choice.text: Will you help me, or will you call him? Voss. He's been looking for me.
choice.speaker: npc

options.text: You're staying here. Hidden. I'll find out what this is.
I'll call Ilse. She promised she'd know.
Voss pays well for lost property.

hidden.text: ...Thank you. I'll be quiet. I'm always quiet. It's everyone else who's loud.
hidden.speaker: npc

ilse.text: Hartmann? ...She's alive? Then maybe I'll be, too.
ilse.speaker: npc

sold.text: No - please - you're like them. You're exactly like them.
sold.speaker: npc

start.text: You've grown. Four rooms, staff, a name. The crews need a ripper who belongs to us. Exclusive. Our chrome, our wounded, our enemies cut slow. In return the whole Belt is safe for you.
start.speaker: npc

options.text: I'm yours. The crews' surgeon.
I treat everyone. Your crews get priority, not ownership.
And if I say no?

crew.text: Good. Rook will bring the first list. Some names on it won't be patients.
crew.speaker: npc

priority.text: Priority. You bargain like a politician. ...Fine. For now.
priority.speaker: npc

insulted.text: Ownership was the polite word, Doctor.
insulted.speaker: npc

standoff.text: Then nothing. For now. You're useful; useful people get second chances. Once.
standoff.speaker: npc

threat.text: Then the Belt gets very unsafe for you.
threat.speaker: npc

start.text: Can we talk? Not as boss and staff. As... you know.
start.speaker: npc

options.text: Always. What's wrong?
Make it quick.

variants.text: Can we talk? Not as boss and staff. You paid for my... you didn't have to do that. So I owe you honesty.

talk.text: You made me put chrome in a kid. I keep seeing her face. I said one rule, and you said fine, and then you didn't. I need to know if that's who we are now.
talk.speaker: npc

options.text: It was wrong. It won't happen again.
I paid your debt when nobody else would. Trust me once more.
That kid would have gone to a butcher. We were the better option.
You work for me. You do what the table needs.

variants.text: You made me put chrome in a kid. I said no and you made me anyway. I keep seeing her face. I said one rule, Doctor. One.

forgive.text: Okay. Okay. I'm holding you to it.
forgive.speaker: npc

doubt.text: ...Maybe. I don't know. I'll stay. For now.
doubt.speaker: npc

start.text: I've been thinking. You've got a room nobody's working in. What if I ran it? Under your name. Your rules. Mine too.
start.speaker: npc

options.text: It's yours to run. Make me proud.
You're not ready.

yes.text: I won't let you down. ...I might let the plumbing down. But not you.
yes.speaker: npc

no.text: Yeah. Maybe not. Ask me again sometime.
no.speaker: npc

start.text: Sit. I owe you the truth and I'm running out of steady days to tell it. THREAD was mine. A lattice that grows along the nerves and smooths the signal. It was meant for epilepsy. Lyra wanted obedience. When they got fevers instead, they buried the trial in the Sump.
start.speaker: npc

options.text: Then we tell everyone. With Moor, at a tribunal.
Can you take it out of Noor?
What would Voss pay to know where you are?
Your secret is safe with me.

variants.text: Sit. You kept a filament in your cold box. Of course you did. You've been looking at my work for weeks. THREAD was mine. A lattice that grows along the nerves and smooths the signal. It was meant for epilepsy. Lyra wanted obedience. When they got fevers instead, they buried the trial in the Sump.

expose.text: A tribunal. Adaeze Moor is honest; that's rare enough to be dangerous. I'll testify. I'm dying anyway.
expose.speaker: npc

cure.text: Maybe. With your hands and my memory. It will be the hardest surgery of your life.
cure.speaker: npc

sell.text: ...I trained you. I trained you, and you're a Lyra doctor after all. Go on. Make your call.
sell.speaker: npc

start.text: I'm going to be honest with you, which should frighten you. Voss bought my debt. He wants your patient lists, your THREAD notes, and you, on a plate. I can sell you, or you can make me an offer.
start.speaker: npc

options.text: Pay off your debt. Three thousand. Then you work for me.
Give Voss fake lists. I'll forge them.
Sell me and I'll find you, Vesna.

bought.text: Three thousand. ...Nobody's ever bought me out, they've only bought me. Fine. I'm yours. Don't make it weird.
bought.speaker: npc

forged.text: Fake lists for a real monster. I like it. He'll be chasing ghosts in the drowned district for a week.
forged.speaker: npc

caught.text: He saw through it. Of course he did. Lock your doors, darling.
caught.speaker: npc

scared.text: ...You would, wouldn't you. Fine. I'll stall him.
scared.speaker: npc

sold.text: Big words. Voss has bigger guards. Sorry, darling. Business.
sold.speaker: npc

start.text: I've counted forty static cases. I have nothing a tribunal will accept. You have the implants, the records, the patients. Will you give them to me?
start.speaker: npc

options.text: Everything. Take it to the tribunal.
For a licence. A real one.
The Undermarket pays better for Lyra secrets.
No. This is too dangerous.

variants.text: I've counted forty static cases, and you have a trial chart with forty beds on it. Beds, doctor. Names. With that, a tribunal can't look away. Will you give it to me?

I've counted forty static cases, and a clerk of mine has been carrying laundry to your door. Don't look like that: I hired her. Forty closed files, your implants, your patients. Together it's a case. Will you give them to me?

given.text: Then it begins. They'll come for both of us now. Thank you, Doctor.
given.speaker: npc

licence.text: A licence. You drive a hard bargain for a saint. ...Done. Board seal by morning.
licence.speaker: npc

sold.text: You sold it. Of course you did. Everyone down here sells everything.
sold.speaker: npc

no.text: Then I'll keep counting. And one day I'll count you.
no.speaker: npc

start.text: Doctor. You've been very busy for a backroom. Give me the girl, your notes and your silence, and you'll have a suite in Meridian Heights by Friday. Refuse, and I'm afraid the Sump will have a fire.
start.speaker: npc

options.text: Accept. A suite sounds nice.
Here's what I've got on THREAD. Walk away, or it's public tomorrow.
Make me your partner instead. I can make THREAD work.
Get out.

accept.text: Excellent. Wear something white. They like white upstairs.
accept.speaker: npc

backs.text: ...You'd really do it. How very inconvenient. Fine. For now, Doctor, you are not worth the paperwork.
backs.speaker: npc

partner.text: A street surgeon who can make THREAD stable. ...Prove it, and the lab is yours.
partner.speaker: npc

fire.text: Such a shame about the wiring in these old buildings.
fire.speaker: npc

start.text: The city doesn't remember surgeons. It remembers what they made of it. So: what did you make?
start.speaker: npc

choose.text: Choose who you are now. Everything you did decides which doors are open.
choose.speaker: npc

options.text: A doctor. People come to me because I keep them alive.
The Undermarket answers to me.
Lyra's surgeon, upstairs, in white.
A network of clinics no one can shut down.
The one who dragged THREAD into the light.
The one who finished what Lyra started.
The surgeon everyone is afraid of.

end.text: Then that's your story. The Sump will tell it wrong, of course. It always does.
end.speaker: npc
